blocks.en_text: When I was first learning to meditate,
blocks.zh_text: 我刚开始学冥想的时候，

blocks.en_text: the instruction was to simply pay attention to my breath,
blocks.zh_text: 指导方法就是单纯地注意自己的呼吸，

blocks.en_text: and when my mind wandered, to bring it back.
blocks.zh_text: 当思绪飘走时，再把它拉回来。

blocks.en_text: Sounded simple enough.
blocks.zh_text: 听起来挺简单的。

blocks.en_text: Yet I'd sit on these silent retreats,
blocks.zh_text: 可我却坐在那些静默闭关中，

blocks.en_text: sweating through T-shirts in the middle of winter.
blocks.zh_text: 大冬天里汗湿了一件又一件T恤。

blocks.en_text: I'd take naps every chance I got because it was really hard work.
blocks.zh_text: 我一有机会就打盹，因为这活儿真的很费劲。

blocks.en_text: Actually, it was exhausting.
blocks.zh_text: 说实话，那真是累人。

blocks.en_text: The instruction was simple enough
blocks.zh_text: 指导方法本身够简单了，

blocks.en_text: but I was missing something really important.
blocks.zh_text: 但我漏掉了一个非常重要的东西。

blocks.en_text: So why is it so hard to pay attention?
blocks.zh_text: 那么，为什么集中注意力这么难呢？

blocks.en_text: Well, studies show
blocks.zh_text: 研究表明，

blocks.en_text: that even when we're really trying to pay attention to something --
blocks.zh_text: 即使我们真的很努力地想专注于某件事——

blocks.en_text: like maybe this talk --
blocks.zh_text: 比如也许就是这场演讲——

blocks.en_text: at some point,
blocks.zh_text: 到了某个时刻，

blocks.en_text: about half of us will drift off into a daydream,
blocks.zh_text: 我们中大约有一半人会走神做起白日梦，

blocks.en_text: or have this urge to check our Twitter feed.
blocks.zh_text: 或者有种冲动想去刷一下Twitter。

blocks.en_text: So what's going on here?
blocks.zh_text: 那这到底是怎么回事呢？

blocks.en_text: It turns out that we're fighting one of the most evolutionarily-conserved
blocks.zh_text: 原来，我们是在对抗科学界目前已知的

blocks.en_text: learning processes currently known in science,
blocks.zh_text: 最受进化保守的学习过程之一，

blocks.en_text: one that's conserved
blocks.zh_text: 这个过程的保守性

blocks.en_text: back to the most basic nervous systems known to man.
blocks.zh_text: 可以一直追溯到人类已知的最基本的神经系统。

blocks.en_text: This reward-based learning process
blocks.zh_text: 这个基于奖励的学习过程

blocks.en_text: is called positive and negative reinforcement,
blocks.zh_text: 叫做正强化和负强化，

blocks.en_text: and basically goes like this.
blocks.zh_text: 基本上是这样的。

blocks.en_text: We see some food that looks good,
blocks.zh_text: 我们看到一些看起来不错的食物，

blocks.en_text: our brain says, "Calories! ... Survival!"
blocks.zh_text: 大脑就说：“卡路里！……生存！”

blocks.en_text: We eat the food, we taste it --
blocks.zh_text: 我们吃掉食物，尝到味道——

blocks.en_text: it tastes good.
blocks.zh_text: 味道不错。

blocks.en_text: And especially with sugar,
blocks.zh_text: 尤其是糖，

blocks.en_text: our bodies send a signal to our brain that says,
blocks.zh_text: 我们的身体会向大脑发送一个信号，说：

blocks.en_text: "Remember what you're eating and where you found it."
blocks.zh_text: “记住你在吃什么，以及你在哪儿找到的。”

blocks.en_text: We lay down this context-dependent memory
blocks.zh_text: 我们就这样留下了这种依赖情境的记忆，

blocks.en_text: and learn to repeat the process next time.
blocks.zh_text: 并学会下次重复这个过程。

blocks.en_text: See food,
blocks.zh_text: 看到食物，

blocks.en_text: eat food, feel good,
blocks.zh_text: 吃掉食物，感觉很好，

blocks.en_text: repeat.
blocks.zh_text: 重复。

blocks.en_text: Trigger, behavior, reward.
blocks.zh_text: 触发、行为、奖励。

blocks.en_text: Simple, right?
blocks.zh_text: 很简单，对吧？

blocks.en_text: Well, after a while, our creative brains say,
blocks.zh_text: 过了一阵子，我们富有创造力的大脑就说：

blocks.en_text: "You know what?
blocks.zh_text: “你知道吗？

blocks.en_text: You can use this for more than just remembering where food is.
blocks.zh_text: 你可以用这个做的不只是记住食物在哪儿。

blocks.en_text: You know, next time you feel bad,
blocks.zh_text: 你看，下次你感觉不好的时候，

blocks.en_text: why don't you try eating something good so you'll feel better?"
blocks.zh_text: 干嘛不试试吃点好东西让自己感觉好一点呢？”

blocks.en_text: We thank our brains for the great idea,
blocks.zh_text: 我们感谢大脑出了个好主意，

blocks.en_text: try this and quickly learn
blocks.zh_text: 试了一试，很快就学到

blocks.en_text: that if we eat chocolate or ice cream when we're mad or sad,
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们生气或难过时吃巧克力或冰淇淋，

blocks.en_text: we feel better.
blocks.zh_text: 就会感觉好一些。

blocks.en_text: Same process,
blocks.zh_text: 同样的过程，

blocks.en_text: just a different trigger.
blocks.zh_text: 只是换了个触发点。

blocks.en_text: Instead of this hunger signal coming from our stomach,
blocks.zh_text: 不再是来自胃里的饥饿信号，

blocks.en_text: this emotional signal -- feeling sad --
blocks.zh_text: 而是这种情绪信号——感到难过——

blocks.en_text: triggers that urge to eat.
blocks.zh_text: 触发了吃东西的冲动。

blocks.en_text: Maybe in our teenage years,
blocks.zh_text: 也许在我们十几岁的时候，

blocks.en_text: we were a nerd at school,
blocks.zh_text: 我们在学校里是个书呆子，

blocks.en_text: and we see those rebel kids outside smoking and we think,
blocks.zh_text: 看到外面那些叛逆的孩子在抽烟，我们就想：

blocks.en_text: "Hey, I want to be cool."
blocks.zh_text: “嘿，我想变酷。”

blocks.en_text: So we start smoking.
blocks.zh_text: 于是我们开始抽烟。

blocks.en_text: The Marlboro Man wasn't a dork, and that was no accident.
blocks.zh_text: 万宝路牛仔可不是个呆子，这绝非偶然。

blocks.en_text: See cool,
blocks.zh_text: 看，酷，

blocks.en_text: smoke to be cool,
blocks.zh_text: 抽烟显得酷，

blocks.en_text: feel good. Repeat.
blocks.zh_text: 感觉好。重复。

blocks.en_text: Trigger, behavior, reward.
blocks.zh_text: 触发、行为、奖励。

blocks.en_text: And each time we do this,
blocks.zh_text: 每次我们这样做，

blocks.en_text: we learn to repeat the process
blocks.zh_text: 我们就学会了重复这个过程

blocks.en_text: and it becomes a habit.
blocks.zh_text: 然后它就变成了习惯。

blocks.en_text: So later,
blocks.zh_text: 所以后来，

blocks.en_text: feeling stressed out triggers that urge to smoke a cigarette
blocks.zh_text: 感到压力大就会触发想抽根烟的冲动

blocks.en_text: or to eat something sweet.
blocks.zh_text: 或者想吃点甜的东西。

blocks.en_text: Now, with these same brain processes,
blocks.zh_text: 现在，靠着同样的大脑机制，

blocks.en_text: we've gone from learning to survive
blocks.zh_text: 我们从学会生存

blocks.en_text: to literally killing ourselves with these habits.
blocks.zh_text: 变成了用这些习惯实实在在地害死自己。

blocks.en_text: Obesity and smoking
blocks.zh_text: 肥胖和吸烟

blocks.en_text: are among the leading preventable causes of morbidity and mortality in the world.
blocks.zh_text: 是世界上可预防的致病和致死主要原因之一。

blocks.en_text: So back to my breath.
blocks.zh_text: 所以回到我的呼吸。

blocks.en_text: What if instead of fighting our brains,
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们不去跟自己的大脑较劲，

blocks.en_text: or trying to force ourselves to pay attention,
blocks.zh_text: 也不去强迫自己集中注意力，

blocks.en_text: we instead tapped into this natural, reward-based learning process ...
blocks.zh_text: 而是利用这种自然的、基于奖励的学习过程……

blocks.en_text: but added a twist?
blocks.zh_text: 但加一点变化呢？

blocks.en_text: What if instead we just got really curious
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们只是变得非常好奇，

blocks.en_text: about what was happening in our momentary experience?
blocks.zh_text: 好奇我们当下这一刻的经历里正在发生什么？

blocks.en_text: I'll give you an example.
blocks.zh_text: 我给你们举个例子。

blocks.en_text: In my lab,
blocks.zh_text: 在我的实验室里，

blocks.en_text: we studied whether mindfulness training could help people quit smoking.
blocks.zh_text: 我们研究了正念训练能否帮助人们戒烟。

blocks.en_text: Now, just like trying to force myself to pay attention to my breath,
blocks.zh_text: 就像我试图强迫自己关注呼吸一样，

blocks.en_text: they could try to force themselves to quit smoking.
blocks.zh_text: 他们也可以试着强迫自己戒烟。

blocks.en_text: And the majority of them had tried this before and failed --
blocks.zh_text: 他们大多数人以前都试过，而且失败了——

blocks.en_text: on average, six times.
blocks.zh_text: 平均六次。

blocks.en_text: Now, with mindfulness training,
blocks.zh_text: 而用正念训练，

blocks.en_text: we dropped the bit about forcing and instead focused on being curious.
blocks.zh_text: 我们去掉了强迫的部分，转而专注于保持好奇。

blocks.en_text: In fact, we even told them to smoke.
blocks.zh_text: 事实上，我们甚至让他们去抽烟。

blocks.en_text: What? Yeah, we said, "Go ahead and smoke,
blocks.zh_text: 什么？对，我们说：“去抽吧，

blocks.en_text: just be really curious about what it's like when you do."
blocks.zh_text: 只是要非常好奇地体会抽烟时到底是什么感觉。”

blocks.en_text: And what did they notice?
blocks.zh_text: 他们注意到了什么？

blocks.en_text: Well here's an example from one of our smokers.
blocks.zh_text: 这里有个我们一位吸烟者的例子。

blocks.en_text: She said, "Mindful smoking:
blocks.zh_text: 她说：“正念抽烟：

blocks.en_text: smells like stinky cheese
blocks.zh_text: 闻起来像臭奶酪，

blocks.en_text: and tastes like chemicals,
blocks.zh_text: 尝起来像化学药品，

blocks.en_text: YUCK!"
blocks.zh_text: 恶心！”

blocks.en_text: Now, she knew, cognitively that smoking was bad for her,
blocks.zh_text: 她其实在认知上早就知道抽烟对她有害，

blocks.en_text: that's why she joined our program.
blocks.zh_text: 所以才加入我们的项目。

blocks.en_text: What she discovered just by being curiously aware when she smoked
blocks.zh_text: 而她只是通过抽烟时好奇地觉察，就发现了

blocks.en_text: was that smoking tastes like shit.
blocks.zh_text: 抽烟尝起来像屎一样。

blocks.en_text: Now, she moved from knowledge to wisdom.
blocks.zh_text: 于是，她从知识走向了智慧。

blocks.en_text: She moved from knowing in her head that smoking was bad for her
blocks.zh_text: 她从脑子里知道抽烟对她有害，

blocks.en_text: to knowing it in her bones,
blocks.zh_text: 变成了骨子里都明白这一点，

blocks.en_text: and the spell of smoking was broken.
blocks.zh_text: 抽烟的魔咒就被打破了。

blocks.en_text: She started to become disenchanted with her behavior.
blocks.zh_text: 她开始对自己的行为不再着迷。

blocks.en_text: Now, the prefrontal cortex,
blocks.zh_text: 前额叶皮层，

blocks.en_text: that youngest part of our brain from an evolutionary perspective,
blocks.zh_text: 从进化角度看是我们大脑中最年轻的部分，

blocks.en_text: it understands on an intellectual level that we shouldn't smoke.
blocks.zh_text: 它在理智层面上明白我们不该抽烟。

blocks.en_text: And it tries its hardest to help us change our behavior,
blocks.zh_text: 它竭尽全力想帮我们改变行为，

blocks.en_text: to help us stop smoking,
blocks.zh_text: 帮我们戒烟，

blocks.en_text: to help us stop eating that second, that third, that fourth cookie.
blocks.zh_text: 帮我们忍住不吃第二块、第三块、第四块饼干。

blocks.en_text: We call this cognitive control.
blocks.zh_text: 我们把这叫做认知控制。

blocks.en_text: We're using cognition to control our behavior.
blocks.zh_text: 我们用认知来控制自己的行为。

blocks.en_text: Unfortunately,
blocks.zh_text: 不幸的是，

blocks.en_text: this is also the first part of our brain
blocks.zh_text: 这也是我们大脑中

blocks.en_text: that goes offline when we get stressed out,
blocks.zh_text: 在压力大时会最先罢工的部分，

blocks.en_text: which isn't that helpful.
blocks.zh_text: 这可帮不上什么忙。

blocks.en_text: Now, we can all relate to this in our own experience.
blocks.zh_text: 这一点我们都能从自己的经历中体会到。

blocks.en_text: We're much more likely to do things like yell at our spouse or kids
blocks.zh_text: 我们更容易做出冲配偶或孩子大吼这类事，

blocks.en_text: when we're stressed out or tired,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们压力大或疲惫的时候，

blocks.en_text: even though we know it's not going to be helpful.
blocks.zh_text: 哪怕我们知道这样做没什么好处。

blocks.en_text: We just can't help ourselves.
blocks.zh_text: 我们就是控制不住自己。

blocks.en_text: When the prefrontal cortex goes offline,
blocks.zh_text: 当前额叶皮层罢工时，

blocks.en_text: we fall back into our old habits,
blocks.zh_text: 我们就会退回到旧习惯里，

blocks.en_text: which is why this disenchantment is so important.
blocks.zh_text: 这就是为什么这种“祛魅”如此重要。

blocks.en_text: Seeing what we get from our habits
blocks.zh_text: 看清我们从习惯中得到了什么，

blocks.en_text: helps us understand them at a deeper level --
blocks.zh_text: 能帮我们在更深的层面上理解它们——

blocks.en_text: to know it in our bones
blocks.zh_text: 真正从骨子里明白它，

blocks.en_text: so we don't have to force ourselves to hold back
blocks.zh_text: 这样我们就不必强迫自己克制

blocks.en_text: or restrain ourselves from behavior.
blocks.zh_text: 或约束自己的行为。

blocks.en_text: We're just less interested in doing it in the first place.
blocks.zh_text: 我们只是从一开始就没那么想做了。

blocks.en_text: And this is what mindfulness is all about:
blocks.zh_text: 而这正是正念的意义所在：

blocks.en_text: Seeing really clearly what we get when we get caught up in our behaviors,
blocks.zh_text: 真正清楚地看到，当我们陷入某种行为时，我们得到了什么，

blocks.en_text: becoming disenchanted on a visceral level
blocks.zh_text: 在身体感受的层面上对它祛魅，

blocks.en_text: and from this disenchanted stance, naturally letting go.
blocks.zh_text: 然后从这种祛魅的立场出发，自然而然地放下。

blocks.en_text: This isn't to say that, poof, magically we quit smoking.
blocks.zh_text: 这并不是说，噗的一下，我们就神奇地戒烟了。

blocks.en_text: But over time, as we learn to see more and more clearly
blocks.zh_text: 但随着时间推移，当我们学会越来越清楚地看到

blocks.en_text: the results of our actions,
blocks.zh_text: 自己行为的结果，

blocks.en_text: we let go of old habits and form new ones.
blocks.zh_text: 我们就会放下旧习惯，养成新习惯。

blocks.en_text: The paradox here
blocks.zh_text: 这里的悖论在于，

blocks.en_text: is that mindfulness is just about being really interested
blocks.zh_text: 正念其实就是怀着真正的好奇心

blocks.en_text: in getting close and personal
blocks.zh_text: 去贴近、去亲身感受

blocks.en_text: with what's actually happening in our bodies and minds
blocks.zh_text: 我们身心当下实际发生的一切，

blocks.en_text: from moment to moment.
blocks.zh_text: 一刻接一刻。

blocks.en_text: This willingness to turn toward our experience
blocks.zh_text: 这种愿意转向自己体验的态度，

blocks.en_text: rather than trying to make unpleasant cravings go away as quickly as possible.
blocks.zh_text: 而不是急着让不愉快的渴望尽快消失。

blocks.en_text: And this willingness to turn toward our experience
blocks.zh_text: 而这种愿意转向自己体验的态度

blocks.en_text: is supported by curiosity,
blocks.zh_text: 是由好奇心支撑的，

blocks.en_text: which is naturally rewarding.
blocks.zh_text: 好奇心本身就会带来回报。

blocks.en_text: What does curiosity feel like?
blocks.zh_text: 好奇心是什么感觉？

blocks.en_text: It feels good.
blocks.zh_text: 感觉很好。

blocks.en_text: And what happens when we get curious?
blocks.zh_text: 当我们产生好奇心时会发生什么？

blocks.en_text: We start to notice that cravings are simply made up of body sensations --
blocks.zh_text: 我们开始注意到，渴望不过是由身体感觉组成的——

blocks.en_text: oh, there's tightness, there's tension,
blocks.zh_text: 哦，这里有紧绷，这里有紧张，

blocks.en_text: there's restlessness --
blocks.zh_text: 这里有躁动不安——

blocks.en_text: and that these body sensations come and go.
blocks.zh_text: 而这些身体感觉来了又去。

blocks.en_text: These are bite-size pieces of experiences
blocks.zh_text: 这些都是一小口一小块的体验，

blocks.en_text: that we can manage from moment to moment
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以一刻接一刻地应对，

blocks.en_text: rather than getting clobbered by this huge, scary craving
blocks.zh_text: 而不是被这个巨大又可怕的渴望击垮，

blocks.en_text: that we choke on.
blocks.zh_text: 被它噎得喘不过气。

blocks.en_text: In other words, when we get curious,
blocks.zh_text: 换句话说，当我们产生好奇心时，

blocks.en_text: we step out of our old, fear-based, reactive habit patterns,
blocks.zh_text: 我们就走出了过去那种基于恐惧、条件反射式的习惯模式，

blocks.en_text: and we step into being.
blocks.zh_text: 我们进入了存在的状态。

blocks.en_text: We become this inner scientist
blocks.zh_text: 我们变成了内心的科学家，

blocks.en_text: where we're eagerly awaiting that next data point.
blocks.zh_text: 热切地等待着下一个数据点。

blocks.en_text: Now, this might sound too simplistic to affect behavior.
blocks.zh_text: 这听起来可能太简单了，不足以影响行为。

blocks.en_text: But in one study, we found that mindfulness training
blocks.zh_text: 但在有一项研究中，我们发现正念训练

blocks.en_text: was twice as good as gold standard therapy at helping people quit smoking.
blocks.zh_text: 在帮助人们戒烟方面，效果是金标准疗法的两倍。

blocks.en_text: So it actually works.
blocks.zh_text: 所以它确实有效。

blocks.en_text: And when we studied the brains of experienced meditators,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们研究经验丰富的冥想者的大脑时，

blocks.en_text: we found that parts of a neural network of self-referential processing
blocks.zh_text: 我们发现自我参照加工神经网络的一部分，

blocks.en_text: called the default mode network
blocks.zh_text: 也就是所谓的默认模式网络，

blocks.en_text: were at play.
blocks.zh_text: 在起作用。

blocks.en_text: Now, one current hypothesis is that a region of this network,
blocks.zh_text: 目前有一种假说认为，这个网络中的一个区域，

blocks.en_text: called the posterior cingulate cortex,
blocks.zh_text: 叫做后扣带皮层，

blocks.en_text: is activated not necessarily by craving itself
blocks.zh_text: 它的激活未必是因为渴望本身，

blocks.en_text: but when we get caught up in it, when we get sucked in,
blocks.zh_text: 而是当我们陷入其中、被卷进去的时候，

blocks.en_text: and it takes us for a ride.
blocks.zh_text: 它就会带着我们走。

blocks.en_text: In contrast, when we let go --
blocks.zh_text: 相反，当我们放下——

blocks.en_text: step out of the process
blocks.zh_text: 走出这个过程

blocks.en_text: just by being curiously aware of what's happening --
blocks.zh_text: 只是好奇地觉察正在发生的事——

blocks.en_text: this same brain region quiets down.
blocks.zh_text: 这同一个大脑区域就会安静下来。

blocks.en_text: Now we're testing app and online-based mindfulness training programs
blocks.zh_text: 现在我们正在测试基于应用和网络的正念训练项目，

blocks.en_text: that target these core mechanisms
blocks.zh_text: 它们针对这些核心机制，

blocks.en_text: and, ironically, use the same technology that's driving us to distraction
blocks.zh_text: 而且讽刺的是，用的正是让我们分心的同一种技术，

blocks.en_text: to help us step out of our unhealthy habit patterns
blocks.zh_text: 来帮助我们走出不健康的习惯模式，

blocks.en_text: of smoking, of stress eating and other addictive behaviors.
blocks.zh_text: 比如吸烟、压力性进食和其他成瘾行为。

blocks.en_text: Now, remember that bit about context-dependent memory?
blocks.zh_text: 还记得刚才说的情境依赖记忆吗？

blocks.en_text: We can deliver these tools to peoples' fingertips
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以把这些工具送到人们的指尖，

blocks.en_text: in the contexts that matter most.
blocks.zh_text: 在最关键的情境中。

blocks.en_text: So we can help them
blocks.zh_text: 这样我们就能帮助他们

blocks.en_text: tap into their inherent capacity to be curiously aware
blocks.zh_text: 调动他们与生俱来的好奇觉察能力，

blocks.en_text: right when that urge to smoke or stress eat or whatever arises.
blocks.zh_text: 就在想抽烟、压力性进食或别的什么冲动出现的那一刻。

blocks.en_text: So if you don't smoke or stress eat,
blocks.zh_text: 所以如果你不抽烟，也不压力性进食，

blocks.en_text: maybe the next time you feel this urge to check your email when you're bored,
blocks.zh_text: 也许下次你无聊时感到想查邮件的冲动，

blocks.en_text: or you're trying to distract yourself from work,
blocks.zh_text: 或者你想从工作中分心的时候，

blocks.en_text: or maybe to compulsively respond to that text message when you're driving,
blocks.zh_text: 又或者开车时忍不住想回那条短信，

blocks.en_text: see if you can tap into this natural capacity,
blocks.zh_text: 看看你能不能调动这种天生的能力，

blocks.en_text: just be curiously aware
blocks.zh_text: 只是好奇地觉察

blocks.en_text: of what's happening in your body and mind in that moment.
blocks.zh_text: 那一刻你身体和心里正在发生什么。

blocks.en_text: It will just be another chance
blocks.zh_text: 这只会是又一次机会

blocks.en_text: to perpetuate one of our endless and exhaustive habit loops ...
blocks.zh_text: 去延续我们无数个令人精疲力竭的习惯循环……

blocks.en_text: or step out of it.
blocks.zh_text: 或者走出它。

blocks.en_text: Instead of see text message, compulsively text back,
blocks.zh_text: 与其看到短信就忍不住回过去，

blocks.en_text: feel a little bit better --
blocks.zh_text: 感觉好一点——

blocks.en_text: notice the urge,
blocks.zh_text: 注意到那股冲动，

blocks.en_text: get curious,
blocks.zh_text: 产生好奇，

blocks.en_text: feel the joy of letting go
blocks.zh_text: 感受放下的喜悦

blocks.en_text: and repeat.
blocks.zh_text: 然后重复。

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢。
